RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at FDR 5.7e-15, with five input steroids — dihydrotestosterone (17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, CHEBI:16330), androstenedione (CHEBI:16422), dehydroepiandrosterone (CHEBI:28689), testosterone (CHEBI:17347), and 17β-estradiol (CHEBI:16469) — as the hit compounds against 27 pathway members, giving a fold-enrichment of 1430. The Reactome parent pathway Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071) is also enriched (FDR 2.9e-14), as is the more specific Androgen biosynthesis sub-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-193048, FDR 1.1e-12). The m/z-direct Mummichog network analysis independently returns MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.4e-05, 11/11 input steroids overlapping with the network module), with the C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis pathway also scoring strongly (12/12 overlap). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' as the sole significant result (p = 8.391e-06), again with the same five steroids. The two non-steroid inputs — butanone (a short-chain ketone, CHEBI:28398) and sulindac (a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory, CHEBI:9352) — are absent from the steroid hit lists in all three methods, which is chemically coherent because neither contains the C-19/C-18 steroidal backbone. react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of the steroid hormone biosynthesis and androgen-and-estrogen metabolism network. RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at FDR 5.7e-15, with five input steroids — dihydrotestosterone (17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, CHEBI:16330), androstenedione (CHEBI:16422), dehydroepiandrosterone (CHEBI:28689), testosterone (CHEBI:17347), and 17β-estradiol (CHEBI:16469) — as the hit compounds against 27 pathway members, giving a fold-enrichment of 1430. The Reactome parent pathway Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071) is also enriched (FDR 2.9e-14), as is the more specific Androgen biosynthesis sub-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-193048, FDR 1.1e-12). The m/z-direct Mummichog network analysis independently returns MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.4e-05, 11/11 input steroids overlapping with the network module), with the C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis pathway also scoring strongly (12/12 overlap). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' as the sole significant result (p = 8.391e-06), again with the same five steroids. The two non-steroid inputs — butanone (a short-chain ketone, CHEBI:28398) and sulindac (a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory, CHEBI:9352) — are absent from the steroid hit lists in all three methods, which is chemically coherent because neither contains the C-19/C-18 steroidal backbone. Butanone appears only in a weak xenobiotics-metabolism signal in Mummichog. Testosterone (KEGG:C00535) and androstenedione (KEGG:C00280) serve as the primary driver metabolites, occupying central positions as substrates in both the androgen-biosynthesis branch and the aromatase-conversion branch leading to estradiol. The treatment-group perturbation implicates a coordinate shift across the entire steroidogenic axis, consistent with endocrine, gonadal, or oncogenic modulation. Sulindac and butanone are likely bystanders or confounding exposures not mechanistically linked to the steroidogenesis signal.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms converge on a single dominant biological signal: perturbation of the steroid hormone biosynthesis and androgen-and-estrogen metabolism network. RaMP multi-database ORA returns KEGG:map00150 'Androgen and Estrogen Metabolism' at FDR 5.7e-15, with five input steroids — dihydrotestosterone (17β-hydroxy-5α-androstan-3-one, CHEBI:16330), androstenedione (CHEBI:16422), dehydroepiandrosterone (CHEBI:28689), testosterone (CHEBI:17347), and 17β-estradiol (CHEBI:16469) — as the hit compounds against 27 pathway members, giving a fold-enrichment of 1430. The Reactome parent pathway Metabolism of steroid hormones (REACT:R-HSA-196071) is also enriched (FDR 2.9e-14), as is the more specific Androgen biosynthesis sub-pathway (REACT:R-HSA-193048, FDR 1.1e-12). The m/z-direct Mummichog network analysis independently returns MUMM:androgen_and_estrogen_biosynthesis_and_metabolism as its top hit (p = 8.4e-05, 11/11 input steroids overlapping with the network module), with the C21-steroid hormone biosynthesis pathway also scoring strongly (12/12 overlap). MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA confirms KEGG:hsa00140 'Steroid hormone biosynthesis' as the sole significant result (p = 8.391e-06), again with the same five steroids. The two non-steroid inputs — butanone (a short-chain ketone, CHEBI:28398) and sulindac (a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory, CHEBI:9352) — are absent from the steroid hit lists in all three methods, which is chemically coherent because neither contains the C-19/C-18 steroidal backbone. Butanone appears only in a weak xenobiotics-metabolism signal in Mummichog. Testosterone (KEGG:C00535) and androstenedione (KEGG:C00280) serve as the primary driver metabolites, occupying central positions as substrates in both the androgen-biosynthesis branch and the aromatase-conversion branch leading to estradiol. The treatment-group perturbation implicates a coordinate shift across the entire steroidogenic axis, consistent with endocrine, gonadal, or oncogenic modulation. Sulindac and butanone are likely bystanders or confounding exposures not mechanistically linked to the steroidogenesis signal.
